parsed.note_claim: The Falkland Islands have never been part of Argentina at any point in their history, although Argentina has tried to claim them.
parsed.label: PARTIAL
parsed.quote: The islands are believed to have been uninhabited prior to European discovery in the 17th century. Controversy exists over the Falklands' discovery and subsequent colonisation by Europeans. At various times, the islands have had French, British, Spanish, and Argentine settlements.
parsed.reason: The page confirms Argentina maintains a claim and that islands were uninhabited, but also notes Argentine settlements and governance (Vernet appointed by Buenos Aires in 1829), so it does not directly substantiate that they were never part of Argentina.
